legalDecision.question: Whether the imported package-level MIT permission notice must be retained alongside current Apache-2.0 materials.
legalDecision.decidedBy: Repository owner (Winsen Labs). Recorded by an agent at the owner's explicit direction; not an automated determination.
legalDecision.decision: Platos continues to distribute @platos/core under Apache-2.0. packages/core/LICENSE stays byte-identical to the repository Apache-2.0 text, and the upstream MIT copyright and permission notice is retained verbatim in packages/core/NOTICE (the Apache-2.0 s4(d) notice mechanism), which is published in the package tarball.
legalDecision.rationale: MIT grants the right to sublicense, so Apache-2.0 redistribution of the derivative stands on its own. Retaining the upstream notice satisfies MIT's requirement that the copyright and permission notice accompany copies and substantial portions. Placing it in NOTICE rather than LICENSE keeps every publishable package's LICENSE byte-identical to the repository Apache-2.0 text, which is an existing enforced invariant, and uses the Apache-2.0 s4(d) mechanism as intended. Doing both makes the question moot under either reading at no cost to the Apache-2.0 election.
